title: Why Dick Smith Shut His Food Brand While It Still Made Money
conflicts: Charity share: one third of profits planned (just-food 2001) vs all profits (news.com.au 2018) vs an undisclosed percentage (SmartCompany 2012); story attributes 'profits went to charity' and the A$10m figure to Smith. Turnover: A$90m revenue early on (just-food 2001) vs Smith's 2018 claim of a $60m peak falling to $15-16m (The Land); story uses only Smith's 2018 figures, attributed. Profitability: contemporary reports say still profitable, Wikipedia says closed to avoid bankruptcy (unsupported); story follows the reports. First product date implied as 2000 by just-food vs 1999 founding; story gives 1999 and does not date the product.
notes: Funding 'bootstrapped' is inferred: Smith owned the licensing business and no outside investors are reported. news.com.au is cited via its Newstalk ZB syndication because The New Daily blocks automated requests.
